scope: Selection audit of all canonical records and all currently public records against stored eligibility; targeted current primary-source checks for discovered scope conflicts. Not a fresh global recruitment/source audit.

after.special_requirement: Solid tumors must be non-sarcomatous, at least 3 cm, with biopsy and draining-node access. Lymphoma requires nodal stage 2 or greater and at least three nodes of 3 cm. Study-team review of organ function and treatment washouts is required.

Tumor generally 2–7 cm and accessible for repeated biopsy; no significant underlying heart, kidney or liver disease, no abnormal blood cell or platelet counts, and no autoimmune disease. Primary liver-tumor eligibility remains unresolved because the published liver-disease exclusion is ambiguous.
At least one measurable lesion accessible for intratumoral injection and repeated biopsy; the protocol brochure names mast cell tumors, soft tissue sarcomas, melanomas and thyroid carcinomas.
Only superficial tumors accessible for intralesional treatment are considered; the study team must confirm histology and local accessibility.

Tufts must assign the dog to a qualifying cohort: Group A requires newly diagnosed limb-bone osteosarcoma without obvious spread and planned amputation; Group B requires prior amputation and carboplatin or study-drug therapy, with measurable lung, skin/subcutaneous or abdominal metastases and no bone metastases. Organ function, blood counts and concurrent drugs require review.
